clue.text: Visit several stations to go to France regularly

definitions.meaning: to flick between television stations one after another
to make frequent trips across the English Channel to France

explanation.definitionFit: A double meaning: switching between TV channels, or crossing the Channel to France again and again.

clue.text: Listen to Bach's final piece with organ

indicators.note: the final piece of the word Bach is its closing letter

parts.note: the ear is the organ of ...

explanation.surface: A music lover is told to attend to the closing movement of a Bach work played with organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like the musical instrument, but here it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to take in sound, the plain verb for what ears do.

clue.text: Wild Australian period of revelry

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters of the next word are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A rowdy spell of partying by Australians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges AUSTRALIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman midwinter festival gave its name to any time of riotous merrymaking.

clue.text: Hearts held captive by rare Piaf song

indicators.note: the hearts of words are their central letters, here taken from both rare and Piaf

explanation.surface: A rare Edith Piaf song stirs the hearts of a captive audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearts' takes the middle two letters of each of 'rare' and 'Piaf'; 'held captive by' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An operatic solo for one voice is a kind of song.

clue.text: Humble worker shows courage — the woman entering major conflict

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage

indicators.note: one word going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: a war is a major conflict
she refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A lowly employee proves brave when a woman goes off to fight in a great war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the insertion; 'shows' only joins. Bottle for courage is British slang, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle-washer is a drudge doing menial jobs, as in 'chief cook and bottle-washer'.

clue.text: Joiner potentially needs new head for mitring, replacing third one in a month

indicators.note: the third letter of the month is swapped out for the new letters

parts.note: November is a month of the year

indicators.note: the head of the word mitring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A carpenter, or joiner, needs a new head on a mitring tool by some date in the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing third one' swaps the V of NOVEMBER for NM. The surface's joiner is a carpenter; in the definition it is someone who joins a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone outside a club is a possible recruit: a would-be joiner rather than an existing one.

clue.text: A charge for crossing island

parts.note: a toll is a fee paid to cross a bridge or use a road

explanation.surface: Paying a fee to get across to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon is a type of island.

clue.text: Style of columns in one newspaper is crazy at first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
on can mean in, as in 'on the team'

indicators.note: the first letters of the words is and crazy are taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper's column layout is called mad at first sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initials of 'is' and 'crazy'. The i is a UK daily newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionic is one of the classical orders of architecture, known for the scrolls on its column tops.

clue.text: All considered where the measuring weights could be used

definitions.text: where the measuring weights could be used
definitions.meaning: read literally, weights would be put on a set of scales

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'taking everything into account', and read literally it is the place on a set of scales where weights go.

clue.text: Broken lip seen by doctor wrongly providing soothing medication

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor
ill can mean wrongly or badly, as in 'ill-advised'

explanation.surface: A doctor botched treatment of a split lip and handed out a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges LIP, SEEN and GP to make SLEEPINGP; 'by' only joins. ILL for 'wrongly' is the adverb sense, as in 'ill-gotten'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet taken to help one sleep is a calming, soothing medicine.

clue.text: Buzzer frequency generates complaint

parts.note: a bee is an insect that buzzes

explanation.surface: A doorbell's repeated buzzing gives rise to grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzzer' looks like a doorbell or game-show button, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a grievance or grumble.

clue.text: Don't get involved in time off away from company

parts.note: leave is permitted absence from work
alone means without other people around

explanation.surface: Advice to stay out of things while taking a holiday away from the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' suggests a business, but it means other people's presence.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from meddling with something is to let it be, an idiom of non-interference.

clue.text: Snacks made initially from beef, lamb and pork?

indicators.note: taking one thing from another means removing it

parts.note: these are all kinds of meat, so together they are meats

indicators.note: the initial of the word made is its first letter

explanation.surface: Light bites prepared with three kinds of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives M from 'made', and 'from' takes it off MEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal word for food, especially light refreshments.

clue.text: One in church moving to transept

indicators.note: letters that move change position, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worshipper shifts across into the transept of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges TO TRANSEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Protestant is a member of one of the Western churches that broke from Rome, so one in a church.

clue.text: A source of real ale in constant demand

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant in science, such as the speed of light
to ask can mean to demand, as in 'asking price'

explanation.surface: Real ale is always popular with drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins. Real ale is traditional cask-conditioned British beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Traditional beer is served from wooden or metal barrels in which it matures.

clue.text: Takes action when outside court

indicators.note: one piece outside another means it wraps around it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone does something once they are out of the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' signals that the word for 'when' wraps around the abbreviation; the surface reads it as leaving the courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: To act is to do something, so acts is a plain synonym for takes action.

clue.text: Close shave, getting dart points caught in back of the neck

indicators.note: pieces in another word sit inside it, so the neck word is split open

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck
an arrow is a kind of dart
E and S are compass points, east and south
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A barber's shave was nearly a disaster when darts lodged at the nape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does the insertion while 'caught' supplies its own letter; 'getting' only joins. Compass points are a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A close shave is an idiom for a near miss, a lucky escape from danger.

clue.text: Large animal beheaded smallest

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: a word beheaded loses its first letter

parts.note: a beast is an animal

explanation.surface: A huge creature lost its head and became tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' takes the B off BEAST, leaving EAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, meaning of the lowest size or amount.

clue.text: A lovebird displayed strangely uniform colour

indicators.note: something done strangely is done oddly, so the letters are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A pet parrot puts on an odd display of the same colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges A LOVEBIRD; 'displayed' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: This dull greenish-brown is the shade of many military uniforms.

clue.text: Another bud unfortunately dropping to the ground?

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events here throws the letters into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A second flower bud sadly falls off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges ANOTHER BUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthbound can mean heading towards the earth, like something falling; the question mark flags this less common sense.

clue.text: Gold lifted onto a comparatively strange heavy vehicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word reads it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
droller means more odd or amusing

explanation.surface: Gold is hoisted onto a rather odd lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns OR upwards to RO in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A road roller is a heavy machine that flattens road surfaces.

clue.text: Exercise equipment — an ideal feature for a beer festival?

definitions.meaning: gymnastic apparatus of two raised rails side by side

definitions.text: an ideal feature for a beer festival?
definitions.meaning: a joke reading: many pubs or drinking counters set side by side

explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts use twin raised rails, and a beer lover would dream of rows of bars running side by side.

clue.text: Powerless to capture girl that simply must be caught

indicators.note: one word capturing another holds it inside

parts.note: unable means lacking the power to do something
miss is a word for a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A helpless man cannot win over a girl who just has to be caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to capture' signals that the girl is held inside the word for powerless; the surface's 'caught' is a show one must catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A show or event too good to miss is one that must be seen or caught.

clue.text: Whatever happens where New York marathon runners are?

definitions.text: where New York marathon runners are?
definitions.meaning: read as '...', they are taking part in a New York race

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'regardless', and split up it puts runners in a NY event.

clue.text: Note well sensory organ below forehead in large predator

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece below another comes after it

parts.note: the brow is the forehead
NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A creature's ear sits under its brow, worth noting in a big hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' matters because this is a down clue: the note and the organ sit beneath the forehead in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The brown bear is a big carnivore, including the grizzly, so a large predator.

clue.text: Turn towards top person when on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upwards means the letters read in reverse

parts.note: to means towards
a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: Turning towards a celebrity as you climb the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reverses TO and VIP together; 'when' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to swivel or turn on a central point.

clue.text: Duty list requiring men to pitch up with volunteers

indicators.note: pitching something up raises it, reading a down entry upwards

parts.note: OR is short for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A duty roster needs men to turn up alongside volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pitch up' turns OR upwards to RO in this down clue; 'pitch up' looks like 'arrive'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule saying who does which duty when.

clue.text: Departed with key during rental period

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits inside it

parts.note: a let is a period of renting property
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone moved out with the key while the tenancy was still running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts F inside LET.
explanation.definitionFit: Left is the past tense of leave, so it means went away.
